title: One run of a capability probe inside the Polkadot app
description: A record of what a Product could and could not do in one runtime. The key names the runtime by what decides compatibility — the date, the host wire codec, the host SDK version and the OS — because no host API exposes the Polkadot app's own version.

key.description: <date>_codec<wire codec>_host-<product-sdk-host version>_<os>-<major>, e.g. 2026-09-19_codec1_host-0.19.1_android-16. Also the file name.

complete.description: false when the report was cut off or some probes were not run for reasons outside the probe (say which in notes).

source.description: Where the prober's code lives, so any result can be checked against how it was measured.

productId.description: The .dot label the prober ran under. Host state (allowances, product accounts, storage) is keyed by it.

webview.description: Engine version from the user agent. On Android this is the system WebView, updated separately from the Polkadot app — not an app-version proxy.

appVersion.description: The Polkadot app version if a person read it off the phone. No host API reports it.

wireCodec.description: The TrUAPI wire codec the Product spoke. The app must answer the same one or every host call hangs.

sdk.description: Exact package versions the Product was built with.

results.description: Keyed by stable probe id (e.g. web.sensors.geolocation).

title.description: What the probe checks, in words.

evidence.description: Raw output the probe attached: permission states before and after, error bodies. Redacted of addresses and file names.

measures.description: Named limits the probe measured (bytes accepted, seconds taken, counts). Values only; the probe's page says what each name means.

retracted.description: Set when the result measured a defect in the probe, not the host — a wrong fixture, a call that could not succeed. Says what was wrong and where it was fixed. The matrix shows the result struck out, so it is never read as a host finding.
